dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Hi, Kevin, hi. Moira Sullivan. I'll keep it short, it sounds like you've got a busy line there, I could hear it ringing behind you.
A little. Day before Christmas Eve, everybody's got something. What can I do for you, Moira?

It's the storm drain out front of my house. One sixty-three Marsh Street, down the Point. It's been, it's grunting, I don't know how else to say it. It gurgles and it's so slow, and anytime we get a thaw it just backs right up into the, hang on. No, put that down. Sorry. Into the street.
Okay, one sixty-three Marsh. Drain's slow and backs up on the thaw. Is it doing that today, or just when it warms up?

Well it's not raining, there's no storm or anything, that's what gets me. It's dry out. It just sits there. Last few days it warmed up a bit and the snowbank melted and it all ran down and the drain couldn't take it. And the sidewalk is a sheet of mud and grit. Like, a sheet of it. I can't get the stroller, I mean, I can't, [pause] Declan, I said not now.
Mud and grit across the sidewalk, got it. Is the water standing in the road, or is it mostly the silt left behind once it drains off?

Both. It pools up by the grate, a good puddle, and then when it finally goes down it leaves all that gunk. And it keeps happening. I'm not new to this, I've called about this, well, it's just always like this and nobody ever does anything about it.

Understood. Sounds like the catch basin's probably packed with sediment. That's usually a crew with the vacuum truck to clean it out. Let me put this in. Is the grate right in front of the house or at the corner?
Right in front. Right at the curb in front of the house, one sixty-three. Not the corner.
Perfect. So I've got a slow drain, backs up in thaw conditions, sediment on the sidewalk, no active storm. Anything coming out of it, like a smell, or is the water going back up out of the grate?
It comes up a little, yeah, bubbles up and then it settles. No smell really. Just wet and gritty and, ugh, my shoes, honestly. Everybody tracks it in.
Yep, that stuff gets everywhere. Alright, I'll open a work order for the drain cleaning.
Okay. And what date, though? Is there a date on it? Because last time I got told somebody would look and then, I mean, nothing. I just want to know when.

Fair question. With the holiday this week, I'd say it's more likely early in the new year than before Christmas. I'll mark it for the crew supervisor to schedule, and the work order will have a target date on it once it's assigned.
So I won't have a date today.
Not a firm one from me, no. But if you give me a good number I'll make sure it's attached so they can call you when it's scheduled.
It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-four. That's the house line.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-four. Got it. And I'll put the sidewalk silt in the notes so they know to look at that too.
Please. Because if they just come and, you know, do the drain and leave the mud everywhere, I'm, [pause] sorry, Declan, I'm on the phone. Sorry, Kevin.
You're fine. Kids at home for the break?
Yes. Anyway. So you'll call me with the date.
That's the plan. Work order's going in now, one sixty-three Marsh Street, The Point, catch basin cleaning, sediment on the walk. You'll hear back once it's on the schedule.
Okay. I hope so. Thank you, Kevin. Happy holidays.
You too, Moira. Merry Christmas. Take care.
